frequency_question: How often does the US executive branch implement primary or secondary financial cutoffs against major foreign commercial banks within a designated medium-term period when policy signals indicate persistent illicit trade?
membership_rule: Includes cases where the US Treasury Department designates or restricts major international commercial banks for violating specific sectoral sanctions regimes (such as Iran or Russia energy caps). Excludes informal warnings or mere diplomatic demarches without actual financial access restrictions.

cases.name: Bank of China and Eastasiacorp various actions (historical precedent subset)
Standard Chartered and various non-US major bank settlements for Iran sanctions
Turkish Halkbank indictment and sanctions-related enforcement

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.5x)
coverage_note: 4 named primary enforcement events; approximately 6 clear historical confrontation cycles meeting threshold.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller tier-3/4 regional banks which are disciplined more frequently with lesser visibility.
skeleton: Enforcement actions against Tier-1/Tier-2 foreign banks under major geopolitical sanctions acts over past decade
multiplier: 4 hits out of 6 major identified confrontation cycles involving systemic banks and oil/trade embargoes
validity_reason: Based on institutional continuity of US Treasury OFAC enforcement patterns across recent administrations, valid until major structural shifts in the global financial clearing architecture occur.
